title: Understanding is the new bottleneck — Geoffrey Litt, Notion
talk_summary: Geoffrey Litt argues that as agents write more code, human understanding (not correctness checking) becomes the real bottleneck, and presents techniques like explainer docs, quizzes, and microworlds to keep humans in the loop.

takeaways.what_they_do: An agent skill generates a structured explainer for each code change: background/context first, intuition before details, then prose-annotated diffs in logical order rather than raw file order.
Each explainer ends with a 5-question medium-difficulty quiz; the author must pass it before sending the PR for review, acting as a 'speed regulator' against moving faster than understanding.
Agents generate throwaway interactive UIs (timeline scrubbers, step-through visualizers, click-through migration walkthroughs) tailored to one debugging or understanding task, not for shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Agents can write code to help us understand code. Where the point isn't building software to ship, it's building these little micro worlds.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of each human talking to their own private agent, humans and agents share a channel/doc where all communication is visible and commentable, building collective understanding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of me and my PM both talking to our own agents, we're in a shared space, we can see each other's communication.

takeaways.what_they_do: Explainer docs open with a background section teaching the reader the system context (engine, coordinate system, subsystems) and can be personalized to what the reader already knows, before showing the change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It starts by teaching me, 'Hey, here's how the system works.'
